source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-186647:Villager price changes are extremely inconsistent, and completely break in combination with hero of the village | Duplicate:inward:MC-230794:Villager Trading Gives More Loot Than Taken | Relates:inward:MC-268017:Re-curing fully discounted villagers resets/doesn't change discounts on that villager
source_meta._title: The discount for curing a villager is multiplied if the villager is reinfected and cured again

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled, difficulty set to Hard, and the same player performing both cures. Use a roofed and illuminated enclosure containing one librarian villager and no unrelated villagers, zombies, job-site blocks, or active Hero of the Village effect.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, not the fixed version 23w31a or any later version.
Use one single-player identity for the entire procedure because the curing discount is associated with the player who performs the cure.
Create the test world in Creative mode with cheats enabled so the required entities, items, and cleanup commands are available without unrelated survival progression.
Set the difficulty to Hard before allowing a zombie to attack the villager; on Hard difficulty, a villager killed by a zombie converts into a zombie villager instead of being randomly lost.
Prepare two Splash Potions of Weakness, two ordinary Golden Apples, a Villager Spawn Egg, a Zombie Spawn Egg, one Lectern, at least 64 Paper, building blocks, glass, and light sources.
Use an enclosed area with a solid roof so zombies and zombie villagers cannot burn in sunlight, and illuminate the interior to prevent unrelated hostile-mob spawning.
Keep the lectern available to the test villager and complete one trade before the first infection so the villager remains a librarian with the same locked trade throughout both cure cycles.
Do not trade with the villager after recording the first-cure reference price, hit the villager, start a raid, or obtain Hero of the Village before the second cure.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses Java Edition 1.15.2, launch it, and wait for the title screen. Do not use 23w31a or a later fixed version.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left title-screen version label identifies the running game as Minecraft 1.15.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, select the Superflat world type, and disable structure generation if that option is available. Create the world and wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> Allow Cheats: ON -> World Type: Superflat -> Generate Structures: OFF -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a newly generated Creative-mode world on flat terrain, with no village or unrelated villagers nearby.

steps.action: Open the pause menu with Esc, select Options, repeatedly select the Difficulty button until it reads Hard, then select Done and return to the game.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Difficulty: Hard -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The Options menu displays Difficulty: Hard.

steps.action: Set the time to the villager work period. Press T to open chat, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the world is in daytime.

steps.action: Keep the test at the same daytime while assigning the profession. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the doDaylightCycle game rule is now false.

steps.action: Disable natural mob spawning so only the deliberately spawned zombie participates. Press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Spawn eggs continue to work with this rule disabled.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the doMobSpawning game rule is now false.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to obtain building blocks, glass, torches or another light source, one Lectern, one Villager Spawn Egg, one Zombie Spawn Egg, at least 64 Paper, two Splash Potions of Weakness, and two ordinary Golden Apples. Place the spawn eggs, potions, and apples in accessible hotbar slots. Do not select Enchanted Golden Apples.
steps.exact_input: E -> Search Items; obtain: Lectern, Villager Spawn Egg, Zombie Spawn Egg, Paper x64 or more, Splash Potion of Weakness x2, Golden Apple x2, glass, solid blocks, and light sources
steps.success_cue: All listed materials are present in the player's inventory, including exactly the ordinary Golden Apple item needed for curing.

steps.action: Build a small escape-proof chamber with a solid floor, a 3-by-3-block interior, walls at least two blocks high, and a solid roof. Use glass in part of the walls so both entities remain visible. Leave one temporary one-block-high interaction opening in the upper half of a wall while keeping the lower wall block in place. Light the interior and place the lectern on its floor. Ensure there are still at least two unobstructed floor blocks for the villager and zombie.
steps.success_cue: The chamber is roofed and illuminated, its lower wall is continuous so adult mobs cannot walk out, its interior and lectern are visible, and the player can aim through the upper interaction opening.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg and right-click an unobstructed floor block inside the chamber exactly once through the interaction opening.
steps.exact_input: Default use input: right-click once with Villager Spawn Egg
steps.success_cue: Exactly one adult villager is alive inside the chamber, and no other villager is present nearby.

steps.action: Wait for the villager to detect the lectern during the frozen work period. Watch for green particles and the villager changing into a librarian. If it remains unemployed after approximately 30 seconds, break and replace the same lectern and continue waiting; do not add another job-site block.
steps.success_cue: The villager wears the librarian profession appearance and can be interacted with for librarian trades.

steps.action: With paper in the inventory, face the librarian and right-click it to open the trading interface. Locate the novice offer that exchanges a displayed quantity of Paper for one Emerald. Record the displayed paper quantity as the baseline and identify this exact offer as the offer to compare after each cure.
steps.exact_input: Default use input: right-click the librarian; reference offer: Paper -> Emerald
steps.success_cue: The trading interface is open and the baseline paper input quantity for the Paper-to-Emerald offer has been recorded.

steps.action: Complete the Paper-to-Emerald offer exactly once: select that offer, ensure the required paper enters the input slot, and click the Emerald in the output slot. Do not complete any additional trades. Close the trading interface with Esc.
steps.exact_input: Click Paper -> Emerald offer -> click the Emerald output once -> Esc
steps.success_cue: One trade has completed, the villager remains a librarian, and its profession and offers are now locked.

steps.action: Select the Zombie Spawn Egg and right-click an unobstructed floor block inside the chamber exactly once. Verify that the spawned entity is an adult regular zombie. If it is a baby zombie or if more than one regular zombie was spawned, stand within 10 blocks, press T, execute the cleanup command, and repeat this step until exactly one adult regular zombie is present.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once with Zombie Spawn Egg; conditional cleanup command: /kill @e[type=minecraft:zombie,distance=..10]
steps.success_cue: Exactly one adult regular zombie and the one locked librarian are alive together inside the chamber.

steps.action: Allow the regular zombie to attack the librarian. Do not hit either entity and do not proceed merely because the villager has taken damage. Wait until the normal librarian disappears and a zombie villager occupies its place.
steps.success_cue: The chamber contains the original regular zombie plus one zombie villager created from the locked librarian; no normal villager remains.

steps.action: Remove only the attacking regular zombie before starting the cure. Stand within 10 blocks of the chamber, press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter. The entity-type filter must remain minecraft:zombie so the zombie villager is not selected.
steps.success_cue: The regular zombie dies and exactly one zombie villager remains alive in the roofed chamber.

steps.action: Select a Splash Potion of Weakness. Aim through the interaction opening at the zombie villager and right-click once to throw the potion. Avoid throwing it against the outside wall.
steps.exact_input: Default use input: right-click once with Splash Potion of Weakness
steps.success_cue: Gray status-effect particles are visible around the zombie villager, confirming that it has Weakness.

steps.action: Immediately select an ordinary Golden Apple, aim directly at the weakened zombie villager through the opening, and right-click it once. Do not left-click or use an Enchanted Golden Apple.
steps.exact_input: Default use input: right-click once with Golden Apple
steps.success_cue: The zombie villager makes the curing-start sound, begins shaking, and emits red particles.

steps.action: Remain near the loaded chamber and wait for the first cure to finish. Do not attack the entity or leave the world. Continue only when the shaking zombie-villager model has been replaced by the normal librarian model; curing can take approximately three to five minutes.
steps.success_cue: The entity is once again a normal librarian villager and no regular zombie is present in the chamber.

steps.action: Face the cured librarian and right-click to open its trading interface. Locate the same Paper-to-Emerald offer used before infection and record its currently displayed paper input quantity as the first-cure reference value. Do not take the Emerald output or complete any trade.
steps.exact_input: Right-click librarian -> inspect the same Paper -> Emerald offer -> record its displayed paper quantity -> Esc
steps.success_cue: The paper input quantity shown after exactly one cure has been recorded, the interface is closed, and no post-cure trade was completed.

steps.action: Select the Zombie Spawn Egg and right-click an unobstructed floor block inside the same chamber exactly once to begin the reinfection cycle. Confirm it is an adult regular zombie. If it is a baby or an extra regular zombie exists, clean up regular zombies with the specified command and retry until there is exactly one adult regular zombie with the same cured librarian.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once with Zombie Spawn Egg; conditional cleanup command: /kill @e[type=minecraft:zombie,distance=..10]
steps.success_cue: The same librarian that completed the first cure and exactly one adult regular zombie are together in the chamber.

steps.action: Allow the second regular zombie to attack the same librarian. Do not hit either entity. Wait until the librarian has been converted into a zombie villager again.
steps.success_cue: The chamber contains one zombie villager created from the previously cured librarian and the regular zombie that reinfected it; no normal villager remains.

steps.action: Remove only the regular zombie before the second cure. While standing within 10 blocks, press T, enter the command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The attacking regular zombie dies and the reinfected zombie villager remains alive alone in the roofed chamber.

steps.action: Select the second Splash Potion of Weakness, aim through the interaction opening at the reinfected zombie villager, and right-click once to throw it.
steps.exact_input: Default use input: right-click once with Splash Potion of Weakness
steps.success_cue: Gray status-effect particles are visible around the reinfected zombie villager.

steps.action: Immediately select the second ordinary Golden Apple, aim directly at the weakened zombie villager, and right-click it once. Do not left-click the entity.
steps.exact_input: Default use input: right-click once with Golden Apple
steps.success_cue: The zombie villager begins shaking and emitting red particles, confirming that the second cure has started.

steps.action: Remain near the loaded chamber and wait for the second curing process to finish. Do not trade, attack the entity, change player identity, reload in another version, or introduce another villager while waiting. Continue only when the entity changes back into a normal librarian.
steps.success_cue: The same test entity has completed its second cure and is now a normal librarian villager with its locked Paper-to-Emerald offer available for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The same locked librarian has just completed its second cure by the same player, no regular zombie remains, and no trade has been performed since recording the first-cure reference quantity. Hand control to the observation subsystem before opening or completing another trade so it can inspect the Paper-to-Emerald price after the second cure.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce, so the minimum sequence was reconstructed from the description: cure a villager, reinfect the same villager, and cure it again.

The report does not specify game mode, world seed, world type, difficulty, villager profession, or a particular trade. Creative mode, a structure-free Superflat world, Hard difficulty, and a librarian's Paper-to-Emerald trade are practical deterministic choices rather than report requirements.

The plan first creates a locked librarian and infects it to obtain the zombie villager used for the first cure. The report does not state whether its initial zombie villager was naturally generated or created by infecting an established villager.
The image attachment is not available in the supplied report text, so it could not be used to identify the reporter's exact villager profession, trade, enclosure, or displayed price.
The curing duration is variable; proceed based on the entity visibly returning to a normal villager rather than on a fixed timer.
The cleanup commands are execution aids not supplied by the report. Their type filter intentionally selects regular zombies and not zombie villagers.

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.2 in single-player, using a newly created Default-type world with seed -7882263134696652088, structure generation enabled, and commands available. Creative mode is selected as a practical way to execute the supplied teleport command without introducing survival-related setup.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Minecraft Java Edition version 1.16.2 rather than the listed fix version or a current release.
Use a newly created world so the distant target chunks have not already been generated in another Minecraft version.
Do not install datapacks, world-generation modifications, or server plugins that could alter terrain or village generation.
Ensure Generate Structures is set to ON because the reproduction target is part of a generated village.
Enable commands by selecting Creative mode during world creation. If the world-creation screen separately exposes Allow Cheats, ensure it is ON.
Use the exact supplied seed, including its leading minus sign: -7882263134696652088.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation that uses release 1.16.2, start that installation, and wait for the Minecraft main menu to appear. Verify that the lower-left corner of the main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.16.2.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.2 main menu is visible.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World. Use a new world rather than opening or recreating an existing save.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open for a new save.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative so in-game commands are available. If an Allow Cheats control is visible, set it to ON. The world name and difficulty do not affect this reproduction and may remain at their defaults.
steps.success_cue: Creative mode is selected and commands are enabled for the new world.

steps.action: Open More World Options. Select the world seed field, remove any existing contents, and enter the supplied seed exactly, preserving the leading minus sign.
steps.success_cue: The seed field displays exactly -7882263134696652088.

steps.action: In More World Options, leave World Type set to Default and ensure Generate Structures is ON. Do not import custom world-generation settings or add datapacks. Select Done to return to the main world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The new world is configured with the exact seed, Default world generation, and Generate Structures set to ON.

steps.action: Select Create New World. Wait for world creation and the initial loading screen to finish. After the player appears, wait until nearby terrain is rendered and movement or menu input responds normally. The player should be in the Overworld.
steps.success_cue: The player is controllable in a newly generated Overworld using the supplied seed.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open in-game chat. Execute the next command in chat rather than in a server console; therefore, retain the leading slash.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to receive a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's teleport command exactly as supplied, including the dimension, selector, decimal coordinates, yaw, and pitch. Press Enter once to execute it. Do not substitute rounded coordinates or remove the final two rotation values.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the player is teleported to X -135.95, Y 63.00, Z -303308.65 in the Overworld with yaw -178.50 and pitch 22.50; the distant destination terrain begins loading.

steps.action: Release all movement and camera controls so the report-supplied position and viewing rotation are preserved. Wait until the destination chunks, nearby terrain, and village structures have fully rendered. Do not continue while void-colored gaps, missing chunk sections, a loading screen, or unresponsive controls remain.
steps.success_cue: The terrain and village around the supplied location are fully rendered, the scene is stable, and controls respond normally while the player remains at the supplied position and orientation.

steps.action: Without moving the player or turning the camera, briefly open the debug overlay with F3 and verify that the XYZ position is approximately -135.950 / 63.000 / -303308.650 and that the player is in the Overworld. Close the overlay with F3 again so it does not obstruct inspection. If the keyboard requires a function modifier, use Fn+F3.
steps.success_cue: The supplied destination and Overworld dimension have been verified, the debug overlay is closed, and the player remains at the report-specified position and orientation beside the loaded target village terrain.

stor.handoff_condition: The teleport command has generated or loaded the target chunks, the village terrain at X -135.95, Y 63.00, Z -303308.65 is fully rendered in Java Edition 1.16.2, and the player remains stationary at the supplied yaw and pitch. Hand control to the observation subsystem for inspection of the generated village path area.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, difficulty, single-player versus dedicated server, or an explicit cheats setting. This plan uses single-player Creative mode solely to provide a deterministic way to execute the supplied command.

Default world type and Generate Structures ON are not explicitly stated in the report, but they are retained because the report concerns naturally generated village terrain and does not provide custom world-generation settings.

The report does not name a particular village building, path segment, or inspection direction beyond the coordinates and rotation embedded in the teleport command. The plan therefore preserves the exact command orientation and does not direct the executor to move before observation.

The report does not explicitly state that the target chunks must be newly generated. A fresh world is used because generating the village in another version or with altered world-generation settings could change the test state.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-248331:The "minecraft:woodland_mansion/1x2_a2" structure generates with one dehydrated farmland block
source_meta._title: One farmland block in plains_large_farm_1 has moisture level 0

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.2, unmodified single-player client using the integrated server, in a Creative-mode Overworld with commands/cheats enabled. A Superflat world is recommended solely to provide a clear, level placement area.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.2, the first version listed as affected.
Use a world without mods or data packs that replace the built-in minecraft:village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1 structure template.
The player must be in Creative mode and able to execute commands.
Use a clear area with enough unobstructed space for a large plains-village farm; a newly created Superflat world is the simplest deterministic choice.
Do not use the report's /place template command in 1.16.2. The /place command was introduced later, so the same built-in template must be loaded through a structure block in this recommended version.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, select and start the Java Edition installation for version 1.16.2. Do not use the listed fix version or a newer release.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu version text identifies the running game as Minecraft 1.16.2.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new world. Set Game Mode to Creative, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and select the Superflat world type under More World Options. Then create the world.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON; World Type: Superflat
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a flat Overworld and can fly by double-tapping Space.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally. Move away from any existing obstruction so the structure has open space around the player.
steps.success_cue: A level, unobstructed placement area is visible and the surrounding chunks are fully rendered.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter to obtain a structure block.
steps.success_cue: A Structure Block is added to the player's inventory or hotbar, and the command does not produce an unknown-command or permission error.

steps.action: If the Structure Block is not already in the nine-slot hotbar at the bottom of the screen, press E to open the inventory and move it into an empty hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E, then select that hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The Structure Block is shown in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top surface of the flat ground and right-click once to place the Structure Block.
steps.success_cue: A Structure Block is placed on the ground directly in front of the player.

steps.action: Aim at the placed Structure Block and right-click it to open its configuration interface.
steps.success_cue: The Structure Block interface is open and shows a mode button, structure-name field, position fields, and load/save controls.

steps.action: Click the mode button in the lower-left portion of the interface repeatedly until the block is in LOAD mode. The button may initially display DATA or another mode.
steps.success_cue: The Structure Block interface visibly identifies its current mode as LOAD.

steps.action: Click the Structure Name field and replace its contents with the built-in template path. For the 1.16.2 Structure Block interface, use the path without the default minecraft namespace prefix.
steps.success_cue: The Structure Name field contains exactly village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1.

steps.action: Set the three Relative Position fields to X=0, Y=1, and Z=0 so the detected template begins one block above the Structure Block rather than overwriting it during the initial placement operation.
steps.success_cue: The Relative Position fields display 0 for X, 1 for Y, and 0 for Z.

steps.action: Leave rotation at 0 degrees and mirroring disabled. Set Structure Integrity to 1.0 so every block stored in the template is loaded; leave the integrity seed at its default value.
steps.success_cue: The interface shows no rotation, no mirror transformation, and an integrity value of 1.0.

steps.action: Click the LOAD button in the lower-right once. This first activation detects the named built-in template and prepares its dimensions rather than being the final trigger.
steps.success_cue: The template is found: its size fields become populated and/or a bounding-box outline is prepared, with no message stating that the structure is unavailable.

steps.action: If the first LOAD activation closed the interface, right-click the same Structure Block again. Confirm that it remains in LOAD mode, still names village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1, and now has detected size values. Do not alter the template name, rotation, mirror, integrity, or relative position.
steps.success_cue: The prepared LOAD interface is open and retains the detected template dimensions and configuration.

steps.action: Click the lower-right LOAD button a second time to place the prepared plains_large_farm_1 template. Perform no further block interaction after this click.
steps.success_cue: The large plains-village farm template is visibly present at the prepared location, including its crop plots, irrigation channels, and composters.

stor.handoff_condition: The second Structure Block LOAD activation has just completed and minecraft:village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1 is present in the world. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without breaking, placing, tilling, jumping on, or otherwise interacting with any farmland block.
uncertainties: The report's exact command, /place template minecraft:village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1, is usable in the affected 1.19-era versions but not in the recommended first affected version, 1.16.2, because /place was introduced in Java Edition 1.19. The plan therefore uses the version-compatible Structure Block loading procedure while preserving the same built-in template.
The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, or world type. Creative mode, cheats, and a Superflat world are practical execution choices rather than reported requirements.

The Structure Block name field uses village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1 because minecraft is the default namespace. This refers to the same template identified in the report as minecraft:village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1.

The report does not identify the target farmland block's exact position within the template. Locating and evaluating that block belongs to the observation subsystem and is intentionally not added to these reproduction steps.
Farmland can receive later game-tick updates after placement. The handoff is therefore immediate, but no gamerule changes are introduced because the report does not require them.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-227469:Leatherworker villagers use the lava cauldron or powder snow cauldron produces water sounds | Relates:inward:MCPE-43961:Villagers lose their job site association with cauldrons filled with lava
source_meta._title: Cauldrons filled with water, lava or powder snow cannot be used as a workstation for villagers

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w45a in a newly created local single-player world. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled. For deterministic isolation, use a Superflat world with structure generation disabled so that no naturally generated villagers or workstation blocks can interfere. Lock the time during villager working hours before placing the workstation.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 20w45a for the primary reproduction.
Use a newly created world rather than a world upgraded from another version.
The player must be in Creative mode and permitted to execute commands.
Use an isolated test area with no other cauldrons or villager workstation blocks nearby.
Use an adult, unemployed villager that has never completed a trade. Do not complete a trade with the villager during setup, because trading can permanently lock its profession.
The primary reproduction uses water, which is explicitly included in the original Steps to Reproduce and is available in the recommended version.
The empty cauldron must be accessible to the villager; do not surround it with blocks that prevent the villager from approaching it.
Unless controls have been rebound, E opens the inventory, T opens chat, number keys or the mouse wheel select a hotbar slot, right-click performs Use Item/Place Block, and Esc closes an interface.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses Java Edition snapshot 20w45a, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running version as 20w45a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, enable cheats, select the Superflat world type, and disable structure generation. These settings isolate the villager from unrelated job-site blocks; they are execution choices rather than requirements stated by the report.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON; World Type: Superflat; Generate Structures: OFF
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode, cheats enabled, Superflat terrain, and structures disabled.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until the player can move normally and the nearby flat terrain has fully rendered.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a responsive, fully rendered Superflat world with no generated village or workstation blocks nearby.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the time command with the leading slash, and press Enter. This places the villager within its daytime work schedule.
steps.success_cue: The world is visibly daytime and the command completes without an error message.

steps.action: Press T, enter the gamerule command with the leading slash, and press Enter to prevent time from advancing out of the work period during setup.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without an error, and daylight remains fixed while setup continues.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and the hotbar is visible at the bottom.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory search to locate a Cauldron, then place one Cauldron into an empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Cauldron item is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Clear or replace the inventory search, locate a Villager Spawn Egg, and place it into a different empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Villager Spawn Egg is visible in the hotbar in a slot different from the Cauldron.

steps.action: Search for a Water Bucket and place it into a third hotbar slot. Leave at least one hotbar slot empty so the villager can later be checked without holding an item.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Cauldron, a Villager Spawn Egg, and a Water Bucket, and at least one hotbar slot remains empty.

steps.action: Press E or Esc to close the inventory and return to the world.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and the player can look and move normally.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Cauldron. Aim at the top surface of a ground block in the open test area and right-click once to place the empty cauldron.
steps.success_cue: One empty cauldron is standing on the ground with open space beside it for a villager.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg. Aim at the ground directly beside the cauldron and right-click once to spawn one villager.
steps.exact_input: Right-click with Villager Spawn Egg selected
steps.success_cue: One adult villager is standing next to the empty cauldron. No other villagers or workstation blocks are present in the test area.

steps.action: Do not place or remove any blocks. Wait while keeping the villager and cauldron loaded until the villager claims the empty cauldron as its job site. Do not continue merely after an arbitrary delay; continue only after the villager changes from unemployed clothing to the leatherworker profession appearance. Green claim particles may also briefly appear.
steps.success_cue: The villager has changed into a leatherworker while the cauldron is still empty.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the player's hand holds no item.
steps.success_cue: The active hotbar slot is empty and no item is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at the villager and right-click once to open its trading interface. Use the interface only to confirm that it is identified as a leatherworker. Do not click a trade offer and do not complete any trade.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the villager with an empty hand
steps.success_cue: The trading interface identifies the villager as a leatherworker, and no trade has been completed.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the trading interface without trading.
steps.success_cue: The world view is restored; the untraded leatherworker and its empty cauldron remain visible.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Water Bucket. Aim the crosshair at the cauldron's interior or upper surface.
steps.success_cue: The Water Bucket is visible in the player's hand and the crosshair is positioned on the empty cauldron.

steps.action: Right-click the empty cauldron once with the Water Bucket to fill it. Perform no additional interaction after this click before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The cauldron visibly contains water and the item in the player's hand has become an empty Bucket.

stor.handoff_condition: The previously claimed empty cauldron has just been converted into a water-filled cauldron by the right-click in step 18, and the same untraded villager is still nearby. Begin observing the villager's workstation association and profession state without performing another player interaction.
uncertainties: The report does not require a particular game mode, world type, seed, or server configuration. Creative single-player, Superflat terrain, and disabled structures are practical choices that remove unrelated workstation blocks and item-acquisition steps.
The report does not specify the time of day. Locking the time at 3000 is a practical measure intended to keep the villager within working hours while it claims the empty cauldron.
The primary plan uses water in 20w45a because water is explicitly present in the original reproduction and 20w45a is the first listed affected version.
The original description also names lava. A separate lava trial can use the same setup in 20w45a, replacing the Water Bucket with a Lava Bucket only at the final fill action.

Powder snow is explicitly added by the report's 20w46a comment. To test that variant, rerun the procedure in 20w46a or another listed affected version that supports the required powder-snow interaction and replace the final fluid with powder snow. The exact historical powder-snow acquisition and cauldron-filling controls were not externally verified.
No external web verification was needed for the primary water reproduction because the supplied report contains the affected versions and complete trigger sequence.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition on PC, using a vanilla single-player world hosted by the integrated server. Prepare the bed-and-villager state in 26.1 Snapshot 2, then preserve and open that same world in the affected version, 26.1 Snapshot 3. Use Creative mode with commands enabled. A dedicated server, multiple players, specific seed, coordinates, resource pack, or datapack is not required by the report.
preconditions: Use a disposable test world rather than an important existing world.

Have launcher installations available for both 26.1 Snapshot 2 and 26.1 Snapshot 3. Snapshot 2 is used only to create the pre-existing bed state clarified by the reporter; Snapshot 3 is the affected version under test.

Ensure both installations use a game directory from which the same saved test world can be opened, or otherwise copy the complete saved world from the Snapshot 2 saves directory to the Snapshot 3 saves directory without changing its contents.
Use an unmodified vanilla client with no mods or datapacks that alter villagers, points of interest, beds, time, dimensions, or mob AI.
Set Particles to All, or at least do not use a particle setting that hides the green villager claim particles needed as a setup confirmation.
Keep only one villager and one bed in the immediate test area. Avoid generated villages or other nearby beds so ownership of the target bed is unambiguous.

Do not break, move, rotate, or replace the target bed after it has been claimed in Snapshot 2. Replacing the bed is explicitly excluded because the report says replacement restores normal sleeping functionality.
Remain close enough to keep the test area actively simulated when setting the time to night.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, enable snapshot versions if they are hidden, and create or select an installation for Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 2.
steps.exact_input: Launcher -> Installations -> enable Snapshots -> New installation -> Version: 26.1 Snapshot 2 -> Create
steps.success_cue: An installation that launches 26.1 Snapshot 2 is visible in the launcher.

steps.action: Create or select a second launcher installation for the affected version, Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 3.
steps.exact_input: Launcher -> Installations -> New installation -> Version: 26.1 Snapshot 3 -> Create
steps.success_cue: Separate launcher installations are available for 26.1 Snapshot 2 and 26.1 Snapshot 3.

steps.action: Launch the 26.1 Snapshot 2 installation and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running game as 26.1 Snapshot 2.

steps.action: Configure a new single-player test world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled. For a deterministic empty test area, select Superflat generation, disable generated structures if that option is available, and use Peaceful difficulty. Name the world so it can be positively identified after changing versions.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> World Name: MC-305691 -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Commands: On -> Difficulty: Peaceful -> World Type: Superflat -> Generate Structures: Off
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is configured for a Creative test world named MC-305691, with commands available and no intended nearby village structures.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain is rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the newly created Snapshot 2 world, surrounding chunks are rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Construct a small open test enclosure on the flat ground so the villager cannot wander away. Make the enclosure approximately 7 by 7 blocks internally, surround it with a wall at least two blocks high, and leave the interior unobstructed and open to the sky. Do not place beds, bells, or job-site blocks other than the single target bed added later.
steps.exact_input: Open Creative inventory with E -> search for a solid block such as Stone -> move it to the hotbar -> select it -> right-click to place a two-block-high perimeter wall
steps.success_cue: An enclosed, unobstructed test area exists with enough floor space for one bed and one villager, and there are no other village points of interest inside it.

steps.action: Obtain one bed from the Creative inventory and put it in the hotbar. Use only one bed in the test area.
steps.exact_input: Press E -> Search Items -> enter: White Bed -> move one White Bed to a hotbar slot -> press E to close the inventory
steps.success_cue: One White Bed is present in the hotbar and no other bed has been placed in the test area.

steps.action: Select the bed's hotbar slot and place it on the floor near the center of the enclosure. Leave clear floor beside it and at least two blocks of unobstructed vertical space above both halves of the bed.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing the White Bed -> aim at the enclosure floor -> right-click once
steps.success_cue: Exactly one complete bed is placed inside the enclosure and is unobstructed so a villager can pathfind to it.

steps.action: Obtain a Villager Spawn Egg from the Creative inventory and place it in the hotbar.
steps.exact_input: Press E -> Search Items -> enter: Villager Spawn Egg -> move the Villager Spawn Egg to a hotbar slot -> press E to close the inventory
steps.success_cue: A Villager Spawn Egg is available in the hotbar.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg and spawn one villager on the floor one or two blocks from the bed. Use the spawn egg on the ground rather than on an existing villager, and do not spawn additional villagers.
steps.exact_input: Select the Villager Spawn Egg's hotbar slot -> aim at the ground one or two blocks from the bed -> right-click once
steps.success_cue: Exactly one adult villager is visible inside the enclosure near the single bed.

steps.action: Stay near the enclosure and wait for the villager to detect and claim the bed. Do not break the bed, place another bed, or leave the world before the claim indication occurs.
steps.success_cue: Green particles are visibly emitted by the villager, confirming the target bed has been claimed while the world is still running in 26.1 Snapshot 2.

steps.action: After the green claim particles have appeared, save the world and return to the title screen. This preserves the claimed bed and villager as pre-existing world data.
steps.exact_input: Press Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The game has returned to the menu and the MC-305691 world is no longer actively loaded.

steps.action: Create a backup of the saved Snapshot 2 world before opening it in another snapshot. Do not load or modify the backup during this reproduction attempt.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select MC-305691 -> Edit -> Make Backup
steps.success_cue: The game reports that a backup was completed, or a corresponding backup archive is present in the backups directory.

steps.action: Exit the Snapshot 2 game client completely so the launcher can start the affected version without the old client retaining the world.
steps.success_cue: The Snapshot 2 client is closed and the Minecraft Launcher is available.

steps.action: Launch the installation for the affected version, 26.1 Snapshot 3, and wait for its main menu.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running game as 26.1 Snapshot 3.

steps.action: Open the same MC-305691 world that was created and saved in Snapshot 2. If a snapshot or world-upgrade warning appears, select the option that creates a backup if necessary and continues loading the existing world; do not create a new replacement world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select MC-305691 -> Play Selected World -> if prompted, choose the option to back up and continue loading
steps.success_cue: The original MC-305691 world has loaded in 26.1 Snapshot 3 rather than a newly generated world.

steps.action: Wait until surrounding chunks have rendered and player movement and mob animation respond normally. Verify that the original villager and original bed remain inside the enclosure. Do not touch, break, move, rotate, or replace the bed.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the upgraded Snapshot 3 world, the original villager is active, the original bed remains in its original position, and the area is fully loaded.

steps.action: Position the player just outside or above the enclosure, close enough to keep the villager simulated and with an unobstructed view of both the villager and the bed. Do not interact with either one.
steps.exact_input: Use movement controls W/A/S/D and, in Creative mode, Space to fly as needed
steps.success_cue: The villager and the full bed are simultaneously visible, and the player remains within the immediate test area.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat input while remaining near the enclosure.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input is open and ready to receive text.

steps.action: Set the Overworld clock to night using the 26.1 Snapshot 3-compatible time command. Include the leading slash because the command is being executed through in-game chat, then press Enter exactly once.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted, chat closes, and the Overworld changes to nighttime while the original villager and original bed remain loaded nearby.

stor.handoff_condition: The same world created in 26.1 Snapshot 2 is now loaded in 26.1 Snapshot 3; the original villager and its previously claimed bed remain present and have not been broken or replaced; the player is nearby with both in view; and /time set night has just been accepted. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately without placing another bed or interacting with the villager or existing bed.
uncertainties: The report does not identify the exact older version in which the existing bed was originally placed. This plan uses 26.1 Snapshot 2 because it is the immediately preceding snapshot and therefore the simplest deterministic interpretation of 'placed before ... snapshot 3.'

The reporter clarified that the bed predated Snapshot 3 but did not explicitly say whether the villager also predated Snapshot 3. This plan preserves both the claimed bed and the claiming villager across the version change to retain the complete state described before the save/rejoin step.

No seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, or game mode was supplied. Creative Superflat with structures disabled and Peaceful difficulty is a practical isolation choice, not a claimed bug requirement.

The original steps permit either leaving and re-entering the area or saving and rejoining the world. This plan uses the save-and-rejoin route because it also performs the version transition required by the reporter's clarification.
The report gives no maximum time for the initial bed claim. The executor must use the stated green particles as the readiness condition rather than advancing after an arbitrary fixed delay.

External verification was limited to official minecraft.net information confirming the snapshot versions, launcher snapshot availability and backup warning, and the changed but compatible /time set night syntax in 26.1 Snapshot 3.
